post_reset_observation.interpretation: P9E controlled entry trial is device-observed. Video starts with armed ID=2/CRC=47CCACB5, shows the E entry-only kernel selected, then screen loss, Lenovo/Android splash and return to the P9E menu. The separate photo, identified by the user as first reader reentry after that reboot, shows frozen ENTRY and NOW VALID: DBGC=0x43474244, next=size=0x2b264, whole-console CRC=0x8b79118f, logical/raw counts=6/12, latest ID=2/phase=10/CRC=0xf17e59fc. ARM has one logical and one raw hit with matching prior CRC=0x47ccacb5; KERNEL_ENTRY has one of each with CRC=0xf17e59fc and SCTLR_EL1=0xc00808 (M=0). Reconstructing phase-10 record bytes from ID/value/prior header reproduces the photographed CRC. New reader invocation ID=3/query=0/armed=0 and read-only status confirm capture before new Query/ARM. PRE_MMU, POST_MMU, MAP_FAILURE and RESET_RETURN have zero hits, expected for E. The valid header and same-session entry record survived one observed reboot; actual reset-source attribution, M execution and sustained MMU-on remain unverified.

launch_display_observation.interpretation: P9M launch photo confirms menu identity J716F V23P9M KERNEL TRACE r1 and the M entry/pre-MMU/post-MMU kernel item, with stage DARWIN BOOT, a green top band, and visible DARWINBOOT text: inputs validated; exiting boot services. Do not infer MMU progress or a specific stopping PC from the still image or reboot alone.

unarmed_second_launch_observation.evidence_kind: User-supplied handoff photo and direct user clarification; raw photo private
unarmed_second_launch_observation.visible_handoff_text: DARWINBOOT: inputs validated; exiting boot services
unarmed_second_launch_observation.interpretation: User clarifies that after the first user-reported automatic M reboot, the M kernel was launched a second time directly, without a fresh Query/ARM or a supplied first post-reboot reader capture. User reports this second launch remains stopped; the supplied photo shows DARWINBOOT inputs validated; exiting boot services. Source stage1 requires an immediately preceding valid phase-9 ARM cookie, and branches to the WFE halt if append validation fails. If the first launch consumed ARM by appending ENTRY or later records, the unarmed second launch would be rejected; this is a source-supported explanation, not a confirmed device stopping PC. Neither first-run MMU progress nor second-run rejection is established without retained reader records. The second launch must not be treated as a freshly armed M trial.

recovery_reader_observation.status_line: Read only. Photograph ENTRY before Query or ARM.
recovery_reader_observation.interpretation: M recovery reader photo shows frozen ENTRY and NOW VALID: DBGC=0x43474244, next=size=0x2c0d8, whole-console CRC=0xc0749332, logical/raw counts=6/12, latest ID=2/phase=10/CRC=0xdc7aa441. Frozen ARM has one logical and one raw hit, CRC=0xc2c22d94 and cookie=0x50394b45524e454c, exactly matching the M prelaunch baseline. KERNEL_ENTRY has one logical and one raw hit, CRC=0xdc7aa441, SCTLR_EL1=0xc00808 (M=0); reconstructing the record with prior header 0x2c098 reproduces that CRC. PRE_MMU, POST_MMU, MAP_FAILURE and RESET_RETURN all have zero hits. New reader invocation ID=3/query=0/armed=0 with read-only status confirms no new Query/ARM in the snapshot. This recovery capture follows the user-reported first automatic reboot, an unarmed second launch that stalled, and the requested hardware recovery; it is not the missing immediate first-reboot capture, and recovery method/timing is not independently captured. It establishes a surviving M-session entry record and consumed ARM, with no retained later checkpoints. Source requires ARM immediately before entry: the now-visible consumed chain supports second-launch gate rejection, but does not prove the exact PC of that launch. The missing PRE record spans original firstcpu code, pre-hook stack handling, mapping checks/setup/barriers and PRE append; it does not isolate an SCTLR/MMU failure or a reset source.

id3_single_trial_photo_observation.interpretation: Fresh M session ID=3 photo sequence supplies ARM preparation, M handoff display and a new read-only reader invocation. ARM photo: NOW VALID next=size=0x2c218, logical/raw counts=11/17, ID=3/query=1/armed=1, CRC=0x671d1670, PSCI_VERSION=0x00010001, FEATURES=0. Frozen rows still describe prior ID=2, as designed. M launch photo identifies entry/pre-MMU/post-MMU terminal SYSTEM_RESET and shows the DarwinBoot handoff prompt. Subsequent reader photo: ENTRY/NOW VALID next=size=0x2c258, whole-console CRC=0x8b348f61, logical/raw counts=12/18, latest ID=3/phase=10/CRC=0xd1afe339. Frozen ID=3 ARM and KERNEL_ENTRY each have one logical/raw hit; ARM CRC=0x671d1670 matches prelaunch, ENTRY CRC=0xd1afe339 and SCTLR_EL1=0xc00808 (M=0). Both displayed CRCs reconstruct from the record format and prior headers. PRE_MMU, POST_MMU, MAP_FAILURE and RESET_RETURN again have no hits. New invocation ID=4/query=0/armed=0 confirms a fresh read-only snapshot. Photos were supplied in response to the requested single-launch/immediate-reader sequence; they independently establish the fresh chain and ENTRY-only repeat, while continuous reboot timing, reset source and absence of all intervening operations are not video-verified. Further identical M retries are not required before adding finer probes. Missing PRE spans original firstcpu, pre stack conversion, map_console and PRE append, not a demonstrated MMU-enable failure.
